title: Bluetooth widget in a panel doesn't react to middle mouse button
line: Middle-clicking a standalone widget in a panel, like Bluetooth, now does its middle-click action, such as turning Bluetooth on or off.
explanation: Widgets outside the system tray use the shell's default compact representation, whose mouse area calls secondaryActivated on a middle click. The mouse area never set acceptedButtons, so it only received the left button and middle clicks fell through to the panel; the tray has its own item that accepts the middle button, which is why the tray icon worked. The change makes the mouse area accept the middle button too.

commits.message:
desktoppackage: let the default compact representation get middle clicks

The mouse area of the default compact representation handles the middle
button by calling secondaryActivated, but it only accepted the left one,
so middle clicks never reached it. Accept the middle button as well.

BUG: 511538

 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

@@ -69,6 +69,7 @@ Kirigami.Icon {
 
         anchors.fill: parent
         hoverEnabled: true
+        acceptedButtons: Qt.LeftButton | Qt.MiddleButton
         onPressed: wasExpanded = defaultCompactRepresentation.plasmoidItem.expanded
         onClicked: mouse => {
             if (mouse.button === Qt.MiddleButton) {

2.53.0

media.caption: Pure master: after middle-clicking the standalone Bluetooth widget (far right) Bluetooth is still on, as the tooltip said it would turn off
With the fix: the same middle click turns Bluetooth off (widget dimmed, tray Bluetooth icon gone); a second one turns it back on

review.text: DefaultCompactRepresentation already handled the middle button in onClicked but never accepted it; adding acceptedButtons is the obvious one-line fix and matches what the tray item does. The change in middle-click behaviour on desktop icons is intended by the bug. Before/after show Bluetooth toggling.
